OPEN SOURCE · v0.9.1 ALPHA

Scattered documents go in.
Your model gets the right information.

MESA turns large, scattered document collections into lasting memory for your AI. When a question comes in, it finds what matters, picks the current version and hands it to your model as the right context.

FROM DOCUMENTS TO YOUR MODEL

One memory between your archive and your model.

YOUR DOCUMENTS

  • policies/
  • contracts/2026/
  • product-notes.md
  • support-tickets/
  • meeting-notes.txt
  • regulations/
  • training/
  • faq.md

Many files, many versions, different teams.

MESA

  1. AddDocuments enter once, with their source.
  2. SplitText becomes searchable passages; with a model, facts are extracted too.
  3. Keep versionsA change creates a new revision; the current one wins.
  4. Search four waysMeaning, words, facts and relationships, within what the app may read.
  5. Rank and limitResults are combined and trimmed to fit the model.

CONTEXT FOR YOUR MODEL

How many days do customers have to return a product?

  • “Returns are accepted within 30 days.”policies/returns.txt · v2
  • “Refunds go back to the original payment method.”support-guide.md · v5
  • “Opened software cannot be returned.”policies/returns.txt · v2

Your model writes the answer from this context.

THE PROBLEM

The more documents you have, the harder the right one is to find.

A language model only knows what is in front of it. A whole archive does not fit into a prompt, so something has to pick the right passages every time.

  • The whole archive does not fit.
  • Uses an outdated document.
  • Forgets what it learned yesterday.

01MEMORY

A large archive, organised

MESA keeps your documents as searchable passages, so the model gets the relevant part, not the whole archive.

Only what matters reaches the model.

See the architecture →

02REVISION

The current version wins

When a document changes, searches return the new version once it is processed. The old one stays in history.

MESA numbers every revision.

See it in the example →

03SOURCE

Every answer has a source

Your assistant can show which document and which passage supports what it says.

MESA returns the passage and its document.

How search works →

IN ONE MINUTE

How MESA works, in three steps.

  1. 1

    Add your documents

    Text files, notes, policies. MESA keeps the text and where it came from.

    mesa add policy.txt
  2. 2

    MESA prepares them

    It splits each document into passages and makes them searchable in the background.

  3. 3

    Ask, and get the passage

    Your application asks a question. MESA returns the matching passage, its document and version.

    mesa search "returns"

Good to know: your own model writes the answer. MESA gives it the right text.

Follow the document lifecycle →

WHEN IS IT USEFUL?

When your application needs your information.

A company assistant

Finds answers in procedures, product documents and team notes.

A research tool

Shows which document and passage supports a finding.

An agent with memory

Looks up previously saved notes in later conversations.

Legal teams

Searches legislation and court decisions and shows the exact passage. Built on MESA Data and MESA Law, which are still in development.

BEFORE YOU TRY IT

What works, and what you need.

Text input
The CLI reads UTF-8 text files. Convert PDF and Word files to text first.
Local data
Data is stored in ~/.mesa/data. Models and external providers are off by default; this is not a full network-isolation guarantee.
Optional models
Meaning search and fact extraction need a model provider, which can receive data and charge for use.
Size limit
The document HTTP API accepts up to 5,000,000 UTF-8 bytes per request.
